builder_plan.scenario: An assistant chooses the wrong API or sends arguments your product cannot use.
builder_plan.change: Apply the proposed tool-selection or argument-generation change in a sandbox.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current agent with the same tool schemas and task budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct completed actions, invalid calls, retries, latency, and cost per completed task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Agentic LLM reasoning in pediatric diabetes outcome prediction from multimodal medical records
summary: Replaces trained task-specific ML classifiers for clinical outcome prediction with an LLM pipeline that cites chart evidence and self-audits its reasoning. Costs include API inference per patient over multimodal records, prompt and audit-pipeline engineering, and dependence on third-party model behavior, with no training compute required. Failures can include residual citation mismatches, degradation on outcomes with more training data where ML may be competitive, API cost scaling with cohort size, and unvalidated generalization outside this pediatric diabetes setting.
rationale: The AUROC gain over trained ML on small cohorts is achievable with API-only infrastructure, but the single-domain retrospective evidence and auditability requirements justify a workload-specific pilot rather than direct production adoption.
technique: Evidence-citing self-auditing LLM pipeline for clinical risk prediction

claims.statement: Replaces trained task-specific ML classifiers for clinical outcome prediction with an LLM pipeline that cites chart evidence and self-audits its reasoning. Costs include API inference per patient over multimodal records, prompt and audit-pipeline engineering, and dependence on third-party model behavior, with no training compute required. Failures can include residual citation mismatches, degradation on outcomes with more training data where ML may be competitive, API cost scaling with cohort size, and unvalidated generalization outside this pediatric diabetes setting.
Pooled AUROC 0.815 vs 0.656-0.700 (T2D) and 0.756 vs 0.603-0.631 (T1D) against trained ML; 4 of 70,246 cited values mismatched the chart; physicians agreed with CEDAR in ~9 of 10 cases.
